questions.prompt: A red blood cell bursts when placed in pure water, but a plant cell kept in pure water does not. Which structure explains the difference?

options.label: A
options.text: The cellulose cell wall, which resists the extra water pressure
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Water enters both cells by osmosis. The plant cell has a tough cellulose cell wall outside its membrane; as water enters, the wall resists the pressure, so the cell becomes firm (turgid) but does not burst. The red blood cell has no wall, so it swells and bursts. (The nucleus controls cell activities but cannot pump out water; chloroplasts make food and do not absorb the inflow; plant and animal cell membranes are similarly thin.)

options.label: B
options.text: The nucleus, which pumps water out of the plant cell
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: The chloroplasts, which absorb the extra water
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: The cell membrane, which is thicker in plant cells
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: Water enters both cells by osmosis. The plant cell has a tough cellulose cell wall outside its membrane; as water enters, the wall resists the pressure, so the cell becomes firm (turgid) but does not burst. The red blood cell has no wall, so it swells and bursts. (The nucleus controls cell activities but cannot pump out water; chloroplasts make food and do not absorb the inflow; plant and animal cell membranes are similarly thin.) Therefore the correct answer is A: The cellulose cell wall, which resists the extra water pressure.

questions.prompt: Pieces of peeled cassava are placed in a concentrated salt solution. After one hour the pieces have become soft and have shrunk slightly. Which statement explains this?

options.label: A
options.text: Water moved by osmosis from the salt solution into the cassava cells
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Water moved by osmosis from the cassava cells into the stronger salt solution
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Osmosis moves water across a partially permeable membrane from the weaker (more dilute) solution to the stronger (more concentrated) one. The concentrated salt solution draws water out of the cassava cells, so they lose turgor and the pieces go soft. (Water moving in would make the pieces firm, not soft; salt does not dissolve the cell contents.)

options.label: C
options.text: Salt moved into the cells and dissolved their contents
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: The cassava absorbed salt, which made the cells firm
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: Osmosis moves water across a partially permeable membrane from the weaker (more dilute) solution to the stronger (more concentrated) one. The concentrated salt solution draws water out of the cassava cells, so they lose turgor and the pieces go soft. (Water moving in would make the pieces firm, not soft; salt does not dissolve the cell contents.) Therefore the correct answer is B: Water moved by osmosis from the cassava cells into the stronger salt solution.

questions.prompt: State two structural differences between a typical plant cell and a typical animal cell.
questions.correctAnswer: A plant cell has a cellulose cell wall and chloroplasts (and usually a large central vacuole); an animal cell has none of these structures.
questions.workedSolution: A typical plant cell is surrounded by a cellulose cell wall, contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis and usually has one large central vacuole. An animal cell has only a cell membrane, no chloroplasts and only small temporary vacuoles. Any two of these differences earn the marks. Answer: plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts (and a large central vacuole); animal cells do not.

questions.prompt: A diagram of a cell measures 45 mm across. The real cell is 0.15 mm across. Calculate the magnification of the diagram.
questions.workedSolution: Magnification = size of image ÷ real size of object = 45 mm ÷ 0.15 mm = 300. The diagram is 300 times larger than the real cell. Answer: ×300.

questions.prompt: Ama is studying how substances move into and out of cells.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define the term diffusion.
parts.correctAnswer: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until they are evenly spread (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State two factors that affect the rate of diffusion.
parts.correctAnswer: Any two of: temperature — a higher temperature gives faster diffusion (1); the concentration difference (gradient) between the two regions (1); the distance over which diffusion must occur; the size of the particles (1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why a tiny organism such as Amoeba does not need a special transport system, but a human being does.
parts.correctAnswer: Amoeba is microscopic, so oxygen and nutrients reach every part of its single cell by diffusion over a very short distance (1). A human is large and made of many cells, so diffusion alone would be far too slow; a blood circulatory system is needed to carry materials quickly to all cells (1).

questions.prompt: Why does the wall of the left ventricle of the heart have thicker muscle than the wall of the right ventricle?

options.label: A
options.text: It receives blood from both lungs at once
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: It pumps blood a shorter distance to the lungs
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: It must pump blood at higher pressure round the whole body
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the entire body, a long distance that needs high pressure, so its muscular wall is the thickest. The right ventricle pumps blood only to the nearby lungs at lower pressure. (Pumping to the lungs is the right side’s job; valves are thin flaps that prevent backflow and do not need thick muscle to support them.)

options.label: D
options.text: It contains more valves that need support
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the entire body, a long distance that needs high pressure, so its muscular wall is the thickest. The right ventricle pumps blood only to the nearby lungs at lower pressure. (Pumping to the lungs is the right side’s job; valves are thin flaps that prevent backflow and do not need thick muscle to support them.) Therefore the correct answer is C: It must pump blood at higher pressure round the whole body.

questions.prompt: During a game of football, Kofi’s breathing becomes faster and deeper. What is the main reason for this change?

options.label: A
options.text: His lungs are resting, so they work more slowly
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: His body temperature falls and the lungs keep him warm
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: His heart stops, so the lungs take over its work
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: His muscles need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide that must be removed
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Exercise raises the rate of respiration in the muscle cells, using up more oxygen and releasing more carbon dioxide. Faster, deeper breathing supplies the extra oxygen and expels the extra carbon dioxide. (The lungs do not rest during exercise; breathing is not controlled by body temperature falling, and the heart beats faster rather than stopping.)

questions.workedSolution: Exercise raises the rate of respiration in the muscle cells, using up more oxygen and releasing more carbon dioxide. Faster, deeper breathing supplies the extra oxygen and expels the extra carbon dioxide. (The lungs do not rest during exercise; breathing is not controlled by body temperature falling, and the heart beats faster rather than stopping.) Therefore the correct answer is D: His muscles need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide that must be removed.

questions.prompt: State two functions of the human skeleton other than giving the body its shape.
questions.correctAnswer: Any two of: it protects delicate organs such as the brain, heart and lungs; it allows movement by providing attachment for muscles; it makes blood cells in the bone marrow; it stores minerals such as calcium.
questions.workedSolution: Besides supporting and shaping the body, the skeleton protects delicate organs (the skull guards the brain and the ribs guard the heart and lungs), provides firm attachment points for muscles so that movement is possible, manufactures red and white blood cells in the bone marrow, and stores minerals such as calcium and phosphorus. Any two of these functions earn the marks.

questions.prompt: After exercising, Esi counts her pulse 21 times in 15 seconds. Calculate her heart rate in beats per minute.
questions.workedSolution: There are 4 × 15 = 60 seconds in one minute, so multiply the 15-second count by 4: 21 × 4 = 84. Answer: her heart rate is 84 beats per minute.

questions.prompt: When 50 cm³ of water is mixed with 50 cm³ of ethanol, the final volume is slightly less than 100 cm³. What does this show about matter?

options.label: A
options.text: Particles of matter have spaces between them, so smaller particles fill gaps between larger ones
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The particle theory says matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them. When water and ethanol mix, some of the smaller particles occupy spaces between the larger ones, so the total volume shrinks slightly. (No measurable evaporation or chemical reaction takes place during the mixing, and matter cannot be destroyed by simply mixing liquids.)

options.label: B
options.text: Some of the liquid always evaporates during mixing
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: The two liquids react to form a solid
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: Matter is destroyed when liquids are mixed
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: The particle theory says matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them. When water and ethanol mix, some of the smaller particles occupy spaces between the larger ones, so the total volume shrinks slightly. (No measurable evaporation or chemical reaction takes place during the mixing, and matter cannot be destroyed by simply mixing liquids.) Therefore the correct answer is A: Particles of matter have spaces between them, so smaller particles fill gaps between larger ones.

questions.prompt: A mixture contains iron filings, sand and common salt. A learner wants a sample of pure salt. Which sequence of separation methods is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Evaporate first, then filter, then use a magnet
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Use a magnet, dissolve the rest in water and filter, then evaporate the filtrate
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. A magnet first pulls out the magnetic iron filings. Adding water then dissolves only the salt; filtering removes the insoluble sand as the residue. Evaporating (or crystallising) the filtrate finally recovers the dissolved salt. (A dry mixture of solids cannot be filtered, and the magnet must be used before dissolving or the filings end up in the filter paper.)

options.label: C
options.text: Filter the dry mixture, then dissolve and evaporate
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: Dissolve everything, filter, then use a magnet on the solution
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: A magnet first pulls out the magnetic iron filings. Adding water then dissolves only the salt; filtering removes the insoluble sand as the residue. Evaporating (or crystallising) the filtrate finally recovers the dissolved salt. (A dry mixture of solids cannot be filtered, and the magnet must be used before dissolving or the filings end up in the filter paper.) Therefore the correct answer is B: Use a magnet, dissolve the rest in water and filter, then evaporate the filtrate.

questions.prompt: State two differences between a mixture and a compound.
questions.correctAnswer: In a mixture the substances keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods; in a compound the elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio and can be separated only by chemical means.
questions.workedSolution: A mixture contains two or more substances that are not chemically joined: each keeps its own properties, the amounts can vary, and the substances can be separated by physical methods such as filtering or evaporation. A compound forms when elements chemically combine in a fixed ratio; it has completely new properties and can be split up only by chemical means. Any two of these differences earn the marks.

questions.prompt: A stone has a mass of 54 g. When it is fully immersed, it raises the level of water in a measuring cylinder from 50 cm³ to 70 cm³. Calculate the density of the stone.
questions.workedSolution: Volume of the stone = 70 cm³ − 50 cm³ = 20 cm³. Density = mass ÷ volume = 54 g ÷ 20 cm³ = 2.7 g/cm³. Answer: the density of the stone is 2.7 g/cm³.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows the energy transformations in a hydroelectric power station such as Akosombo?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrical energy → kinetic energy → potential energy
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Chemical energy of coal → heat energy → electrical energy
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Potential energy of stored water → kinetic energy of moving water → kinetic energy of turbines → electrical energy
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Water held behind the dam has gravitational potential energy; as it falls through the penstock it gains kinetic energy, which spins the turbines, and the generators convert that movement into electrical energy. (A hydroelectric station burns no coal, and the chain cannot begin with electrical energy, which is the output, not the input.)

options.label: D
options.text: Light energy → sound energy → electrical energy
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: Water held behind the dam has gravitational potential energy; as it falls through the penstock it gains kinetic energy, which spins the turbines, and the generators convert that movement into electrical energy. (A hydroelectric station burns no coal, and the chain cannot begin with electrical energy, which is the output, not the input.) Therefore the correct answer is C: Potential energy of stored water → kinetic energy of moving water → kinetic energy of turbines → electrical energy.

questions.prompt: No machine is 100% efficient. What happens to the input energy that is not converted into useful work?

options.label: A
options.text: It is destroyed by the machine
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: It is stored inside the machine forever
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: It changes back into the original fuel
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: It is changed into other forms, such as heat and sound, that are not useful
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. By the law of conservation of energy, energy cannot be created or destroyed. Friction between moving parts converts some of the input energy into heat and sound, which do no useful work, so the useful output is always less than the input. (Energy is never destroyed, and the wasted heat does not turn back into fuel.)

questions.workedSolution: By the law of conservation of energy, energy cannot be created or destroyed. Friction between moving parts converts some of the input energy into heat and sound, which do no useful work, so the useful output is always less than the input. (Energy is never destroyed, and the wasted heat does not turn back into fuel.) Therefore the correct answer is D: It is changed into other forms, such as heat and sound, that are not useful.

questions.prompt: State the law of conservation of energy, and name the energy transformation that takes place when a torch is switched on.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be changed from one form to another. In a torch, chemical energy in the battery changes into electrical energy and then into light (and a little heat).
questions.workedSolution: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed but can only be transformed from one form to another. When a torch is switched on, the chemical energy stored in the battery becomes electrical energy in the circuit, and the bulb converts this into light energy with a small amount of heat.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg bag of rice is lifted from the floor onto a shelf 3 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the potential energy gained by the bag.
questions.workedSolution: Potential energy gained = m × g × h = 2 kg × 10 m/s² × 3 m = 60 J. Answer: the bag gains 60 J of potential energy.

questions.prompt: Two lamps are connected in series in a circuit. One lamp blows (its filament breaks). What happens to the other lamp?

options.label: A
options.text: It goes out because the circuit is now incomplete
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. In a series circuit there is only one path for the current. A broken filament breaks that single path, so no current flows and the second lamp goes out. (In a parallel circuit the second lamp would stay on; a lamp cannot become brighter when the current has stopped completely.)

options.label: B
options.text: It becomes brighter because it gets all the current
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: It keeps shining normally
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: It becomes dimmer but stays on
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: In a series circuit there is only one path for the current. A broken filament breaks that single path, so no current flows and the second lamp goes out. (In a parallel circuit the second lamp would stay on; a lamp cannot become brighter when the current has stopped completely.) Therefore the correct answer is A: It goes out because the circuit is now incomplete.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure the current flowing through a lamp, and how is it connected?

options.label: A
options.text: A voltmeter, connected in series with the lamp
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: An ammeter, connected in series with the lamp
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Current is measured with an ammeter, and because the same current must pass through it, the ammeter is connected in series with the lamp. A voltmeter measures potential difference and is connected in parallel across a component. (An ammeter connected in parallel would create a short circuit across the lamp.)

options.label: C
options.text: An ammeter, connected in parallel with the lamp
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: A voltmeter, connected across the battery only

questions.prompt: Places near the equator are generally hotter than places near the poles. Which statement best explains this?

questions.prompt: State two differences between igneous rocks and sedimentary rocks.
questions.correctAnswer: Igneous rocks form when molten magma or lava cools and solidifies; sedimentary rocks form from layers of deposited sediment that are compacted and cemented. Sedimentary rocks often show layers and may contain fossils; igneous rocks do not.
questions.workedSolution: Igneous rocks, such as granite and basalt, form when hot molten rock (magma or lava) cools and hardens. Sedimentary rocks, such as sandstone and limestone, form when layers of sediment are pressed and cemented together over a long time, so they usually show visible layers and may contain fossils; igneous rocks have neither layers nor fossils. Any two of these differences earn the marks.

questions.prompt: A rain gauge at a school weather station recorded 12 mm, 18 mm and 15 mm of rain on three days. Calculate the total rainfall and the average daily rainfall.
questions.correctAnswer: Total 45 mm; average 15 mm per day
questions.workedSolution: Total rainfall = 12 + 18 + 15 = 45 mm. Average daily rainfall = 45 mm ÷ 3 days = 15 mm per day. Answer: total 45 mm and average 15 mm per day.
